limits: All metrics tables are labelled illustrative; actual benchmarks are in the book's GitHub repository, not the chapter.
No GPU model, problem size, run count or profiler version is given for Tables 10-2 to 10-5.
Persistent-kernel 2-3x and 35% GPU-use figures are asserted without measurement.
Megakernel 1.2-6.7x is quoted from a figure source with no model/GPU/batch in the text; caption says throughput, text says latency.
Prose and code disagree on the warp-specialized compute warp: prose says consumer_release() is called immediately after consumer_wait(), code calls it after compute_full_tile.
Table 10-3 labels the 68/92/96% row 'Warp execution efficiency' while the text calls it SM utilization / SM Active %.
practices: Profile with Nsight Compute first; if memory-bound start with a two-stage pipeline, if compute-bound consider warp specialization or clusters (Key Takeaways).
Add another pipeline stage (STAGES=3) when compute outweighs memory (Key Takeaways; the note flags this as probably backwards).
Use warp specialization for imbalanced or latency-hiding cases; for small or extremely memory-bound kernels stay with double buffering (Warp Specialization section).
Size cooperative grids with cudaOccupancyMaxActiveBlocksPerMultiprocessor and check cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel's return status.
Use grid.sync() sparingly; prefer cluster.sync() and DSMEM for limited cross-block coordination.
Start with clusters of 2 or 4 blocks; larger clusters reduce occupancy.
Every block must reach each cluster.sync() or grid.sync() or the kernel deadlocks.
Use cluster.sync() before map_shared_rank(); choose TMA multicast for large clusters/high reuse, DSMEM sharing for small clusters/tight SMEM.
Verify compiler-generated pipelines (torch.compile, NVCC) before hand-tuning.

terms.definition: a set of techniques that overlap memory operations and computations within a single kernel execution
assigning operations to warps that use different hardware, such as data movement (e.g., TMA) and compute (e.g., Tensor Cores)
terms.where: Warp Specialization and the Producer-Consumer Model

terms.definition: a single, long-running kernel whose threads continually pull work from a shared producer-consumer queue
fuses entire sequences of operations across layers and even across GPUs into a single large kernel
a hardware-level hierarchy; a group of thread blocks guaranteed coscheduled on the same GPC, sharing DSMEM
terms.where: Thread Block Clusters and Distributed Shared Memory

terms.definition: distributed shared memory: extends __shared__ memory across a thread block cluster
on-chip SRAM region used to track coordination metadata such as barrier state for DSMEM and cluster sync
two thread blocks coscheduled in a cluster across SMs within a GPC
